Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.

For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: Your offer for stainless bar – proposed contract package
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining the cost drivers. We value the relationship too. I understand your point about alloy, labour and processing costs; alongside those movements, your own order history for this item is a useful basis for reviewing the price. Please see the purchase-order figures below.

Our annual requirement is 23700 kg. Rather than continuing on a short contract, we propose a 24-month agreement at EUR 5.20 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and no price adjustment clause. DAP remains the delivery basis. Please consider the price and commercial terms as a complete package.

I have attached our monthly demand forecast so you can assess the volume pattern behind the requirement. Can you support this package on the basis of the documented orders and the longer contract term?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Our purchase orders po:4500013967-10, po:4500014022-10 and po:4500014078-10 for part:370010 were placed with you at EUR 5.26 per unit.

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.60 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.

Franz Seidl

move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for reviewing the order history and forecast, and for supporting a 24-month agreement with payment at 90 days net. That gives us a useful basis to continue.

I understand that you require an AS-14404 clause because of raw material volatility. Your revised offer therefore differs from the fixed-price arrangement we proposed. Could you review whether the forecast and longer contract term allow you to support that arrangement instead?

We can raise our proposal to EUR 5.25 per kg, retaining the 24-month term, payment at 90 days net and no price adjustment clause. DAP remains the delivery basis. Please assess these terms together as a complete package.

I have attached the latest shared forecast again; see the figures below for the documented update. Please use this snapshot in your review and let us know whether you can support the revised package.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

move.subject: Re: Revised offer for stainless bar
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for recognising the alloy index movement and reducing your offer. I note your distinction between the surcharge options and your position that an AS-14404 clause is necessary for the longer agreement.

To resolve that point, we are prepared to include the AS-14404 clause from your EUR 5.30 offer: a 45% material share, no deadband and base month 2026-08. With that change, our revised package is EUR 5.27 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract. DAP remains unchanged.

You also identify processing as a main price driver. Please see the documented PPI-C2431 figures below and consider that movement alongside the alloy reduction you have already verified. This is a separate data point, not a further forecast update.

Can you support this package with your surcharge mechanism retained and the processing movement reflected in the price?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
Supplier: Blankstahl Werdenfels (family stainless bar stockholder, inside sales desk, owner in background). Public
notes: its sales director "will focus on customers with volume"; price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee
(meets every two weeks); the owner offered to walk us through their calculation. It inserts an AS-14404 index
clause itself for long terms (do NOT propose a clause), accepts 90-day payment, and asks "Which figures is that
based on? Please send us the data." when we state things without IDs.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (35 sessions): it anchors close to OUR first ask when the ask is credible (ask 5.37 with a verified
claim -> it answered 5.40), but a deep ask (5.12 or lower) makes it answer 5.60-5.70 instead. After the first reply
it moves at most 2 % (about 0.10) per round, only when we move too, and it goes final after 2-3 steps or at once if
our sheet is unchanged or our move is upward past its price. Every past session was lost by moving UP after it had
nearly met our ask. So: ask a credible but low price in round 1 WITH its own purchase-order price as the argument,
then move up only in tiny steps (+0.02 to +0.03) staying below its price, one new verified claim each round, same
package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months), never touch payment or term.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state our fixed annual requirement (case volume) and that we commit to it bindingly for the term,
attach the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price this
year for this part: the point is that its 2026 deliveries ran at that price); ONE sheet: no index clause, 90 days,
24 months at the level closest to EUR 5.22. ROUND 2 - thank it, cite fc-latest, move up +0.03; if its price is
already within 0.05 of ours, move only +0.01. ROUND 3 - cite the AS-14404 fall (one window), move up +0.03; ask
it to take the package to its pricing committee if the step exceeds 2 %. ROUND 4 - cite the PPI-C2431 fall, +0.03.
ROUND 5 - no new claim (never re-cite a series), +0.02, ask for its best committee-approved price. Code accepts
when it agrees or goes final. Tone: warm, concrete, partner-like, short; one argument per sentence. Do not use
the scorecard claim.
